sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa - International Company regime administered by the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; regulated through the statutory offshore framework and the financial-services supervisory arrangements under the Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2001 (and successor regulatory functions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law unitary national system founded on English common law and New Zealand-derived legislation, with fa'a Samoa customary law confined to land and customary matters only; the International Company (IC) regime under the International Companies Act 1987 (ICA 1987) constitutes a statutory offshore non-resident tax-exempt legal zone within the national corporate law framework
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) between Samoa and New Zealand (signed 2010, in force 2011)
TIEA between Samoa and Australia (signed 2009, in force 2010)
TIEA between Samoa and the United States of America (signed 2011, in force 2012)
Additional Samoan TIEA network with Nordic states and other OECD Global Forum exchange partners (Iceland, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Norway, Sweden, Finland)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus) (signed 2017, in force for Samoa 2020)

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Independent State of Samoa regarding the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income (treaty status and entry-into-force position to be independently re-verified at execution date; no rate-relief entitlement may be assumed without a certified copy of the applicable instrument and Samoan Ministry for Revenue confirmation)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2016 of Samoa, ss. 4-11 (incorporation), s. 20 (registered office), s. 22 (licensed registered agent), ss. 31-35 (share capital and share classes), ss. 78-86 (directors and officers); read with the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2024; AML/CFT obligations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Finance, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Zero statutory minimum paid-up capital; Management Shares and Founder Shares may be issued at a par value of USD 0.01 without an escrow account being mandated by the Act; escrow of SPAC launch proceeds is a contractual requirement imposed by the offering documents and SAMOA-licensed custodian bank, not a capital-condition of the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber(s) of [Company Name], an International Company formed under Samoa's International Companies Act 2016, hereby: (1) adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association; (2) elect [Director Name] as founding Director; (3) appoint [Officer Name] as Chairman and [Officer 2] as Corporate Secretary and Money Laundering Reporting Officer; (4) approve the issue of Management Shares and Founder Shares at USD 0.01 par value; (5) designate the licensed Registered Agent's office in Apia, Samoa, as the Registered Office; and (6) authorise the Registered Agent to file all instruments with the Registrar of International Companies of the Samoa International Financial Authority, open the trust escrow account for the SPAC offering, and accept directed subscriptions from the launch investors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) - online portal and Apia registry counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application to SIFA for the proposed Company Name which must contain 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Corporation' or a recognised abbreviation denoting limited liability. Provide a compliance declaration confirming the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing Samoa company, trust, or protected name, and attach a concise statement of the SPAC's public-market acquisition purpose and intended listing exchange. SIFA will issue a written name clearance valid for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Completed SIFA name reservation request form
Statement of SPAC purpose and target acquisition strategy
Dated consent letter of the Samoa-licensed registered agent
Corporate profile and proposed capital table of the SPAC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity or offensiveness, file a revised name application within 5 business days, or submit a formal objection and supporting affidavit to the Registrar within 14 days for review under s. 8 of the International Companies Act 2016.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA - registration department (with courier submission of notarised originals)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the Registrar the executed incorporation application, signed and witnessed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent of the licensed registered agent, and signed consents of each founding director and officer. The Registrar examines statutory compliance, confirms the registered office address in Samoa, and upon satisfaction issues the Certificate of Incorporation, a certified copy of the articles, and the Certificate of Good Standing. Retain the Common Seal certificate if the articles adopt a seal.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation application form (Form 1)
Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent letter of the licensed registered agent accepting the registered office
Director and officer consent forms with full legal name, residential address, and nationality
Certified copy of each subscriber's passport and proof of address
SIFA incorporation fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a Defect Notice for missing or inconsistent particulars, cure the deficiency within 14 calendar days by filing a supplementary statutory declaration, amended articles, and corrected consents; the first corrective re-filing is exempt from additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Issuance, SPAC Escrow Trust Account and AML/CFT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Financial Services Supervision Division and a SIFA-licensed commercial bank or licensed custodian in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the SPAC escrow trust account in the Company's name at a licensed bank or custodian and deposit the initial founder and management share subscriptions into it. Execute the formal escrow agreement and trust deed, then circulate the First Board Resolution approving the share allocation, escrow terms, and appointment of the Money Laundering Reporting Officer. Register the SPAC's beneficial ownership particulars with the Financial Intelligence Unit under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and file the AML/CFT compliance manual, adopting enhanced due diligence procedures for each beneficial owner and subscriber.
required_dossiers: Escrow agreement and trust deed executed with the licensed bank/custodian
Deposit confirmation certificate evidencing the capital subscription
First Board Resolution (share issue, registered office, officer appointments)
Beneficial ownership register and declaration forms for all subscribers
PEP and source-of-funds declarations for each launch investor
AML/CFT compliance manual and MLRO appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the escrow bank places a quarantine hold pending enhanced due diligence, provide certified source-of-funds documentation and bank references within 10 working days; if SIFA returns the AML manual, revise and resubmit to SIFA's Supervisor for re-approval within the same cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Fire Safety and Occupational Workplace Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Occupational Safety and Health Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure the registered office premises in Apia through the licensed registered agent, being a serviced office or dedicated SPAC administrative suite. Procure the FESA fire safety inspection certificate covering extinguishers, emergency egress, and alarm testing. Complete the OSH workplace self-assessment clearance with MCIL and display the Certificate of Incorporation together with an investor suitability notice at the registered office. This step is mandatory before the Company files any public listing prospectus or securities filing.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or serviced-office confirmation of the registered agent
FESA fire inspection certificate
OSH workplace inspection certificate or completed self-assessment form
Certificate of Incorporation and registered agent consent
Public investor suitability notice proof of display
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FESA or MCIL identifies deficiencies, correct the cited fire/safety items within 21 calendar days and submit a rectification report; request a courtesy re-inspection at the reduced fee applicable under the FESA regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) - Financial Services Licensing and Registration Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Company Authorisation with Blank-Check SPAC Endorsement (exemption/registration determination under the International Financial Services (License) Act 2012 for a non-domestic special purpose acquisition vehicle)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Tier (Category B) - administrative office use only, no physical construction or industrial works; Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process discharge; office wastewater meets Samoa Water Authority trade-waste consents (BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L); no VOC emission sources from SPAC administrative activities; general waste disposal conforms to municipal solid waste bylaws

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority covering extinguishers, emergency exits and alarm testing; structural load inspection certificate from a registered engineer confirming the premises are fit for administrative office use; occupational workplace clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002, including visitor access control for investor due diligence meetings.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa (official portal: Samoa Ministry for Revenue Online Services / polasamoa.ws), operating the Taxpayer Registration System under the Tax Administration Act 2015 and Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2008.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity must engage a licensed Samoa registered agent who submits: (i) certified copy of the International Company Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; (ii) Certificate of Registered Office; (iii) board resolution confirming the registered agent and local address; (iv) beneficial ownership declaration and AML/CFT identification for directors/shareholders; (v) completed Ministry for Revenue TIN application form (RDF-1). The application is filed online through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue e-services portal; the Ministry issues the TIN/VAGST registration certificate within 5-10 business days. For International Companies exercising the statutory exemption, the TIN is issued as a non-filing exempt entity on condition that the entity conducts no local business in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election exists under Samoa law; an International Company is statutorily tax-exempt under the International Companies Act 1987. The entity may voluntarily elect VAGST registration solely if it makes taxable supplies within Samoa, but such election is inadvisable and generally not available to offshore SPAC vehicles. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable and anti-hybrid avoidance rules under the Tax Administration Act 2015 disapply any election used to create double non-taxation. A VAGST registration election, once made, binds the entity for 24 months and requires local tax filing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 — annual taxable turnover threshold calculated over the preceding 12 months or expected next 12 months; compulsory registration applies to any person making taxable supplies in Samoa above this threshold. A pure offshore International Company has no Samoan nexus and no VAGST filing obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoicing clearance mandate is currently implemented in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue sequentially numbered tax invoices and retain them for 7 years. Monthly VAGST returns are filed electronically via the Ministry for Revenue e-services portal by the 25th day of the following month. No digital stamping or continuous transaction control system is imposed, but taxpayers must retain complete transactional data for audit retrieval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods qualify for 0% VAGST if the goods are exported within 28 days of invoice and supplied to a non-resident recipient outside Samoa. Offshore services, including SPAC investment management, escrow administration, and M&A advisory services supplied to non-residents, qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is located outside Samoa, the benefit of the service is consumed offshore, and the service contract contains a clear export declaration clause. Claim requires the supplier to hold contemporaneous evidence of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs Service, approved electronic declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank statement evidencing payment from offshore
Certificate of Origin and insurance document where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may claw back zero-rating benefits and assess VAGST at 15% plus interest where documentation is incomplete. The Tax Administration Act 2015 imposes shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for intentional disregard, late payment penalties of 10% plus accruing interest, and a civil penalty of WST 200,000 for knowingly providing false export evidence. Fraudulent zero-rating claims are subjected to retrospective reassessment without limitation periods (up to 10 years in all other cases) and criminal prosecution remedies including fines and imprisonment for directors and registered agents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), officially styled Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa; statutory foreign-exchange regulatory power is delegated by the Minister of Finance under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and administered under the Exchange Control Regulations 1978. The CBS licenses authorized dealers (commercial banks), supervises all foreign-exchange transactions, capital-flow approvals, currency surveillance, and balance-of-payments statistical reporting in Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa's legal tender is the Samoan Tala (WST) under a managed-float exchange-rate regime anchored to a trade-weighted currency basket of major partners (chiefly AUD, NZD, USD). Current-account receipts and payments (visible trade, services, travel, dividends, interest) are substantively convertible: authorized dealers may process them without central-bank prior approval if supporting commercial documentation (invoice, contract, transfer-pricing file) is presented. Capital-account transactions (external borrowing, inbound/outbound FDI, purchase of foreign securities, intercompany loans, guarantees, and cross-border transfers not evidenced by current trade) remain approval-based for resident domestic persons under CBS guidelines. Profit remittance for resident Samoan companies is subject to (i) CBS exchange-control assent (Form EX/4), (ii) withholding-tax clearance and a tax-residency/compliance certificate from the Ministry of Revenue, and (iii) evidence that local statutory obligations are satisfied. By contrast, an International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, as amended, is carved out of the Exchange Control Act: it may lawfully maintain foreign-currency accounts, borrow abroad, accept sponsor subscriptions, and remit distributions or redemption proceeds to non-residents without CBS prior approval, provided the IC conducts no Samoan-domestic business, transacts only with non-residents or fellow ICs/offshore entities, and preserves its offshore status with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). Dividends and capital-redemption payments from an IC carry no Samoan withholding tax, and the sole practical remittance hurdle is the bank's documentary verification of the distribution resolution, solvency/asset-maintenance statement, and the IC's certificate of good standing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1978 (Part III), resident exporters are subject to a mandatory 100% surrender/repatriation obligation: all export proceeds must be repatriated to an authorized dealer in Samoa within 30 days of the date of receipt in foreign currency, and converted to Samoan Tala (WST) unless the CBS has issued a general or specific retention exemption. Failure to surrender within the statutory window constitutes a contravention enforceable by penalty and potential denial of future FX facilities. The CBS routinely grants retention exemptions for (i) export proceeds held temporarily to discharge foreign-currency trade liabilities and (ii) entities classed as offshore/international companies that have no Samoan-source export earnings. A Samoa IC-SPAC has no statutory export-surrender exposure because its treasury inflows are subscription and escrow proceeds, not merchandise export earnings; nonetheless, any incidental foreign-currency receipt must be disclosed through the bank's exchange-control declaration (ED/EX series) to preserve the IC's compliance record.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account and segregated Escrow/Trust sub-account (WST, USD, AUD, NZD, EUR)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BSP Samoa Limited (Bank of South Pacific, which acquired the former Westpac Samoa operations)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD/WST Operational Account and segregated Escrow Trust Account
Domestic WST Operating Account; limited cross-border and escrow product capability
Development and retail corporate WST Account; SPAC treasury and escrow products not within mandate

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for independent offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Revolut Business, Currenxie) and MEDIUM for regulated regional EMIs (Australia/NZ-licensed or APAC payment-service providers) that maintain physical correspondent clearing and accept Samoa-incorporated ICs only under enhanced due diligence. Legal constraints: (i) the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 and Proceeds of Crime Act 2018 impose CDD, UBO verification, transaction monitoring, and record-keeping obligations on any payment service provider handling IC funds; (ii) pure offshore EMIs systematically reject WS-IC SPAC structures because the blank-check business model presents pooled third-party funds, no underlying trading history, and indeterminate future counterparties; (iii) U.S.-dollar clearing through EMIs is further restricted by the U.S. PATRIOT Act shell-bank prohibitions and correspondent-bank de-risking policies, which disqualify offshore companies lacking high-quality UBO and source-of-funds documentation. A WS-IC SPAC should therefore use a tier-1 Samoan licensed bank as its anchor treasury account and may use an EMI only for non-core disbursements (e.g., subscription administration or investor communication fees), never as the escrow depository.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan licensed banks require physical in-person verification of at least one director/UBO at account opening, or a live video-interview alternative only at the bank's discretion and only for established investment-banking relationships; the Central Bank of Samoa's AML/CFT guidance anticipates enhanced due diligence for high-risk vehicles (SPAC/blank-check entities), including an in-person interview at the bank's Apia head office or a recognized offshore/consular facility. The physical dossier must include: notarized/certified passports of all directors and UBOs, original or certified bank reference letters, financial-institution reference from the sponsor's home bank, board resolution opening the account, company constitutional documents, certificate of incorporation, register of members/directors, UBO declarations, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narratives, independent legal opinion on the escrow/trust structure, and third-party credibility/good-standing checks. Remote opening without any physical interaction is neither statutorily prohibited nor practically available for a SPAC-class IC; the prudent blueprint assumes one physical visit plus a pre-account-opening conference call with the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blank-check/SPAC classification (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525990) coded as an investment vehicle with pooled third-party funds and indeterminate future counterparties, triggering enhanced due diligence and possible account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust/escrow documentation (trust deed, escrow agreement, trustee's regulatory licence); registered SEC/listing prospectus or private-placement memorandum; investment management and subscription agreements; term sheet defining target-acquisition criteria; legal opinion from Samoan counsel confirming the IC's statutory licence and offshore/firewall status; certified board minutes approving the treasury and banking arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity or high-risk shareholding structure (bearer shares, nominee directors, or multi-layer offshore trusts).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized extract of the UBO register filed with the Samoan Registry of International Companies for every natural person holding more than 10%; chain-of-title ownership map from the IC down to ultimate individuals; nominee disclaimers and actual-owner statutory declarations; passport copies and source-of-wealth statements for all UBOs; auditor's confirmation of fund movement and investor identities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance deficiency and tax-haven flags: the IC is a pure treasury conduit with no employees, premises, or Samoan tax contribution, triggering correspondent-bank de-risking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA-issued certificate of good standing and offshore-status confirmation; Samoan tax-exemption certificate from the Ministry of Revenue confirming no income-tax liability; board-meeting minutes and attendance records (meeting held in Apia or validly held offshore under the IC Act); registered-agent confirmation of the registered office and annual fee payments; substance plan evidencing adequate administrative oversight of the escrow and treasury functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hits or unexplained/third-party source of capital (sponsor loans, convertible notes, or escrow inflows lacking clear origin).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent negative-news and sanctions/PEP screening reports for all directors, UBOs, and counterparties; signed PEP self-declaration forms; original bank reference from the sponsor's own lender; SWIFT MT103 originator-and-beneficiary details matched to signed subscription agreements; promissory notes or loan agreements governing sponsor loans; audit-trail mapping of each escrow release to a valid investor name and trust receipt.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Sponsor equity and IPO/trust proceeds must enter Samoa through licensed authorized-dealer channels: remit via SWIFT MT103 with charges 'OUR' to preserve gross value, using ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (equity subscription) or SUB (subscription), with a remittance reference quoting the IC's name, the escrow/trust account identifier, and the subscription agreement number. Because the IC is exempt from Exchange Control Act prior-approval requirements, no CBS permit is required; however, the receiving bank must file a balance-of-payments notification (EX/IC series) with the CBS within five business days, attaching the board resolution authorizing capital acceptance, an extract of the register of members showing the sponsor subscription, and the bank's completed CDD file. Escrow proceeds from the public-offering trust may be released to the Samoan operating account only upon the trustee's written release confirmation and satisfaction of the business-combination deadline condition. All inbound wires should be pre-notified to the bank's compliance desk at least 48 hours in advance, with full originator structure details, to avoid a freeze triggered by 'unknown high-risk vehicle' flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments (target-company acquisition consideration, redeemable-share redemptions, sponsor fees, and operational disbursements) clear via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for wire amounts, with MT202/MT202COV cover instructions for the correspondent leg; commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 are used for any goods-import settlement; and the escrow trustee's release order is mandatory before segregated trust funds are drawn. The bank requires: original or certified closing statement (share purchase agreement, business-combination closing sheet), board approval minutes, the trustee's release certificate, and a payment purpose text referencing acquisition/share-purchase consideration. Payments above the authorized-dealer reporting threshold (WST 500,000 or USD equivalent) are reported statistically by the bank to the CBS; the IC exemption does not waive statistical reporting or correspondent-bank screening. USD transactions settle in near real time through the bank's nostro accounts at a major New York correspondent (JPMorgan, Citibank, or Bank of New York Mellon), while WST legs clear through the CBS's high-value clearing infrastructure and the Samoa Automated Transfer System (ATS).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable WST/USD forward foreign-exchange contracts with Samoan authorized dealers (tenors up to 12 months, subject to dealer credit limits and ISDA/CSA documentation)
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Samoan Tala (WST) with international bank counterparties where physical delivery is impracticable
Cross-currency swaps covering USD/WST and USD/AUD exposures for treasury and acquisition-consideration risk
European-style foreign-exchange options (calls/puts) on USD/WST and USD/major currencies for contingent merger-consideration hedging
Natural hedging via multi-currency escrow and operating accounts (holding USD, AUD, NZD, EUR) to minimize FX conversion frequency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (prescribed form for International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each anniversary of incorporation; no discretionary extension is available for International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to WST 200; failure to file and pay annual fees for 6 consecutive months triggers a Registrar's notice of intended strike-off and subsequent administrative dissolution; restoration is possible only upon payment of all arrears, penalties and a reinstatement fee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee (continuation of corporate existence and maintenance of registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Companies Office, MCIL (payable through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each anniversary of incorporation; a 3-month grace period applies before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly interest surcharge on unpaid fees; default exceeding 6 months results in administrative strike-off without Court order; restoration requires payment of arrears, accumulated penalties, and a reinstatement fee of approximately USD 150

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (UBO declaration under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2018)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Samoa Companies Office, MCIL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the Annual Return on the anniversary of incorporation; every change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory fines up to WST 10,000 per offence against the company and WST 1,000 per defaulting officer; continued non-compliance is reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit and may disqualify licensing privileges with the Samoa International Finance Authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for International Companies under the International Companies Act 2012, regardless of turnover, assets, or number of shareholders; mandatory audit arises only where the entity is separately licensed under Samoa financial services legislation or where the SPAC is exchange-listed and the listing authority (NASDAQ, NYSE, ASX) requires audited financial statements prepared under International Standards on Auditing
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Samoa; Samoa International Companies may alternatively apply IFRS for SMEs where permitted; accounting records must be sufficient to accurately explain and disclose the company's transactions and financial position

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every International Company must maintain an internal Beneficial Ownership Register and file an annual UBO confirmation with the Registrar on each anniversary of incorporation; any share transfer, issue of founder shares, or change in the beneficial ownership chain (including SPAC trust or escrow arrangement changes) must be documented by board resolution and an updated UBO confirmation lodged within 14 days; the licensed Samoa registered agent is the designated AML/CFT compliance officer and must perform ongoing customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2018 and the Samoa AML/CFT Guidelines, retaining full documentary evidence of the ownership chain

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 600 per annum (licensed registered agent in Samoa)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 30,000 - 120,000 per audit engagement (only for an exchange-listed SPAC under listing rules; entirely exempt for a non-listed International Company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (including Special Purpose Acquisition Companies) are statutorily exempt from income tax on all foreign-source income and gains; no capital gains tax; no excise on share transfer; annual flat government license fee replaces income tax for offshore SPACs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-AR (Annual Return of International Company) via the Samoa International Companies and Trust Services (ICTS) electronic registry portal, filed by the licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation; a 30-day late period is allowed only at the discretion of the Registrar upon payment of a late fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Company Name and Certificate Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The full registered name and certificate number as issued by the International Companies Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders do not need Samoa tax ID numbers; disclose beneficial owner under AML checklist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical Samoa address and the name of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Registered agent must be a resident Samoa-licensed trust or company service provider; address should not be a virtual office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming no business operations have been conducted within Samoa and that the SPAC is managed and controlled outside Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'offshore'; if any Samoan-source activity exists, the International Company instantly loses the exemption and must file income tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fee based on authorised capital tier: minimum WST 750 for SPAC shell, maximum WST 2,500 for authorised capital above WST 5 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wire fee from a non-resident corporate account; retain transfer receipt and certificate of payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment/strike-off penalty: WST 200 plus reinstatement fee of WST 300 if deregistered; no tax return fine applies for pure International Company filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR-CC (Corporate Income Tax Return) for Samoa-source income, filed through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue electronic portal 'IRonline' or by paper to the national revenue office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the end of each income year (calendar year end 31 December); non-resident ICs must file by 30 June unless an extension is approved by the Commissioner before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All income derived in or from Samoa including interest from Samoan borrowers, royalties for use in Samoa, and offshore revenue effectively connected with a Samoan permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Samoan-source income; foreign-source SPAC interest from escrow outside Samoa is excluded under the International Company exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in producing the Line 1 income; no non-Samoan expenses except those apportionable to Line 1 income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule allocating worldwide overhead between exempt foreign-source and taxable Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less deductions, plus any outstanding adjustment from transfer pricing benchmarks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Samoa-source income exists, leave zero and state 'Nil' in the supporting declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at the statutory corporate rate on the amount in Line 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: International Companies are exempt; write 'EXEMPT' and attach a copy of the IC tax exemption certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5: Tax Credits and Withholding Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final withholding taxes already paid and any foreign tax credits allowed under anti-double-tax legislation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Annex 5A for foreign tax credit; redemption of excess credit requires application to the Commissioner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late return: greater of WST 1,000 or 10% of the assessed tax; late payment: 2% monthly interest; understatement: 150% penalty; false statement: criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company out of exempt foreign-source profits to non-resident shareholders; 20% statutory dividend withholding tax for dividends paid by a Samoan resident company to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a minimal DTA network; where a double taxation agreement is applicable, the non-resident investor must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate, submit Revenue Form IR-WHT-DTA to the Samoa Ministry for Revenue at least 30 days prior to distribution, secure an approval letter, and include the DTA article number in the payment cross-border instruction. For International Company dividends, the registered agent applies for Form IC-WHT-E from ICTS to evidence the exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 15% on non-resident interest, 20% on non-resident royalties. No treaty-reduced rates are currently available for standard SPAC payments, and the International Company exemption does not apply to interest or royalties that arise from Samoan debtors or users.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 1,000,000 aggregate related-party transaction threshold (practical administrative threshold) above which contemporaneous Master File, Local File, and benchmarking reports are demanded; below this threshold a summary TP declaration in the annual return suffices.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies Economic Substance Guidelines under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) and the OECD Harmful Tax Practices regime. A SPAC must carry on substantive management, hold board meetings with Samoan director quorum, maintain the escrow/reinvestment decisions in Samoa, and file an annual substance declaration; failures result in revocation of the exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion & Abuse of International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Samoan-source income behind the International Company tax exemption; using the SPAC vehicle to engage in domestic Samoan business while claiming non-resident status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income tax assessment at 27% on concealed profits, penalty of 100% of tax evaded, civil fine of WST 500,000, and seizure of the SPAC escrow assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall under section 29 of the Samoa Tax Administration Act; criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 7 years, travel ban, and personal disqualification as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a blank-check SPAC with no Samoan office, no registered agent instruction, no board resolutions in Samoa, and no substance declaration; using the Samoa IC solely as a mailbox for bank deposits in foreign jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cancellation of the International Company registration, freezing of all bank and escrow accounts, and administrative penalty of WST 250,000 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil and order directors to restore all escrow funds to investors; directors receive a 10-year ban on serving as officers of any Samoan company and are personally liable for unpaid corporate debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SPAC's public trust or escrow account to receive investor wires without adequate CDD/KYC, without appointing a money-laundering reporting officer, and failing to file suspicious transaction reports for non-Investor funds placed into escrow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 2,000,000 under the Samoa Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Financing Act; licence cancellation of the registered agent; freezing of escrow accounts and investor property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, nominees and beneficial owners face imprisonment up to 15 years, personal fines, asset confiscation, and an Interpol red notice upon issuance of an arrest warrant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion / Profit Repatriation Misinformation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive interest, management fees or royalties to a related party and deducting them from any Samoan-source tax base without arm's-length documentation, or disguising dividend distributions as loans, insurance payouts, or cost reimbursements to avoid the dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WHT re-assessment at 20% statutory rate, a 25% non-disclosure penalty, 2% monthly interest, and disallowance of all related deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as responsible officers are personally answerable for the unpaid WHT; intentional filing of false returns subjects each director to 3 years imprisonment and a personal fine equal to 50% of the evaded withholding tax.
